title: There is no way to drop out of an event on any screen
description: Found by three independent persona reviews of design/journeys (beginner, rec organiser, league organiser). The entire product philosophy rests on withdrawal being free and cheap: RosterEntry.state has 'dropped', the cascade invariants describe sponsor drops removing three people from two courts, INV-4 promotion exists to fill the gap, and a recorded design constraint says a player's name must never be rendered next to failure language BECAUSE dropping out early is the single most valuable social behaviour in the product. Not one screen in 111 lets anybody leave. rec-friends/2's only button is 'I'm in'. home/1 prints 'Are you playing / they need an answer' with exactly one button. entry/2 says 'Nothing to do - see you at 8.' The beginner persona's verdict: 'joining is one tap and leaving is invisible. That's not free, that's a trap door I can't find' - and she said she would text the organiser rather than open the app. This also blocks the promotion/relay journey, which cannot be drawn without a drop to trigger it.
acceptance_criteria: An event screen shows how to withdraw, the withdrawal screen carries no fault language, and the cascade + promotion that follows is drawn including the sponsor relay.

title: Billers integration epic: pickleball-social folds in as the schedule layer, Billers a level above
description: Decision 2026-08-12 with the owner: Pickle Billers (pickleball-score-generator repo, production at picklebillers.com, Firebase pickleball-score-gen) is the umbrella product; the social/scheduling work integrates INTO it. Backend decision: Firestore-native — implement FirestoreScheduleRepository behind the existing schedule_repository.dart interface (feature/schedule-home branch, schedule_first_home flag); the Workers/D1 contract work becomes design reference. The pickleball-social workers.dev app keeps running for the 2026-08-16 Sunday trial until Billers reaches schedule parity, then retires. Sequence: (1) import the two 2026-Q2 city workbooks so the current leagues exist as structured data, (2) FirestoreScheduleRepository + Sunday 6am events, (3) parity + retire the standalone app. Billers debt flagged during exploration: functions/index.js 3,473 lines, app_state.dart 2,711 lines, dual Provider/Riverpod, hardcoded owner email as admin primitive, 80-field match doc.

Deployed.

title: No loading, error, offline or expired-link state exists in 102 screens
description: From the build-readiness review of design/journeys. The deck draws only success paths. Missing: any loading state; any rendering of the nine ApiError codes; any offline state, even though Device.pending_writes and entry_source='offline_sync' exist in the schema and score-entry-at-the-net is the core offline case, and the two-offline-scores-to-disputed path is never drawn; any expired/used/revoked link screen, which is the contract's most-hit error path (profile/4 covers only profiles); any push-denied / browser_tab / iOS add-to-home-screen screen, which exists as prose on rec-friends/4 and nowhere as a screen; the decline-promotion result; the invite_mode='approval' pending state, though the toggle is drawn on groups/7; and the GET /m/{share_token} 'nothing here' page. The reviewer's summary of the whole deck: 'unusually strong on why - every screen cites the invariant it serves and most serve it correctly. What it has not done is draw the states where the system says no.'
acceptance_criteria: Loading, error, offline, expired-link and permission-denied states are drawn and reachable from the journeys that produce them.

title: The undrawn session surface is the flagship guarantee with no design behind it
description: Named by a build-readiness review as one of three blockers. api.md calls the session preview the flagship guarantee and specifies its payloads precisely: POST /sessions with attendance, Feasibility and a sacrifice choice; the late-joiner preview with three options (3.4); the early-leaver preview with four resolutions (3.5); extend; abandon; adopt-event. None is drawn. comp-rr/5 draws a leaver as a banner, not a preview. The reviewer's point is that the payloads are specified well enough to guess the screens, and that guessing is exactly how 'the preview always appears, even when the change is trivial' ships as a dialog nobody reads. Also entirely undrawn and in the same class: IdentityMerge suggest/execute/undo (schema calls it non-deferrable and warns duplicates get WORSE without phone numbers), account sever (sever-preview, INV-6), dispute resolution (accept/escalate/blind adjudicate/decline - disputes/3 jumps straight to the seven-day void), void (4.6), and the waitlist race-loser screen (api.md promises position and historical promotion odds; rec-open/2 never shows number 17).
acceptance_criteria: The session preview, merge, sever, adjudication, void and waitlist-overflow screens exist.

title: Journeys deck cites enum members, endpoints and response shapes the contract does not define
description: From a staff-engineer build-readiness review of design/journeys held against contract/. Verdict was NOT BUILDABLE YET. Four fixed immediately because they were introduced by the deck itself: disputes/2 wrote 'match.state settled -> claim' when schema.md says state may never move backwards except disputed -> settled|voided (a correction re-runs standings and queues a recompute per api.md 4.2, it does not reopen); organiser/4 used Score.source='organiser' when the enum is app|web|offline_sync (the attribution belongs in reported_by_player_id, which it already had); organiser/2 used Notification.category='sub_request' which is not among the twelve members; and home/1 drew an 8-pip seat meter beside the words '14 of 16 in'. Remaining and NOT yet fixed: Channel.kind='push' on signup/2 and entry/5 (enum is fcm_ios|fcm_android|fcm_web|email|relay_via_sponsor); Player.created_via='signup' (enum has account_signup); Round.state='played' (INV-5d has complete, and the same screen's copy says 'settled', a third word); RosterEntryRef.state cannot carry the 'declined' the deck writes; you/4 shows a DUPR of 4.283 into a decimal(4,2) column. Also cited but undefined: GET /home, GET /groups/{id}, /groups/{id}/events, /groups/{id}/members, GET /events/{id}/responses (the whole D28 organiser screen), GET /sessions/{id}?missing=1. And api.md itself references EventSummary, SessionSummary, MatchSummary, VenueRef, SessionPlayerRef and RoundProjection without ever defining them, which Home, invite resolution and every session screen depend on.
acceptance_criteria: Every enum value, endpoint and response shape named in a writes panel exists in the contract, or the contract is amended to add it.
notes: 2026-08-12 polish pass: deck-side state vocabulary unified — screens say Settled everywhere ('6 up, 5 settled', Settled section header); 'played' survives only as a verb and in writes-panel rows that quote the contract verbatim. The contract-side enum fixes (Round.state 'complete' vs screens' vocabulary) still needed.

title: Dispute-as-delete: one player can erase any loss by disputing it and going quiet
description: Found by a 5.0 tournament-player persona whose bracket seeding depends on the rating. Sequence, using only screens as drawn: dispute any loss at disputes/3, then do nothing. disputes/4 auto-voids after seven days, match state goes disputed -> voided, rating_state held -> excluded, and the denominator visibly drops 68 to 67. One participant, zero cost, and by the product's own stated philosophy (dropping/2) nothing anywhere counts how often somebody does it. Repeat on every bad loss. The subtlety: OQ-45 DID rule for a seven-day auto-void, but it ruled it for DEADLOCK - both sides engaged and disagreeing - as the tail of 'one from each side'. It never contemplated ABANDONMENT, where one person disputes and nobody else responds. The screens do not distinguish the two cases and must. Same reviewer also noted adjudication is fully specified in schema.md (blind, uninvolved organiser) and appears on zero screens, so disputes/3's 'ask the other two' leads straight to auto-void with no human path in between.
acceptance_criteria: Abandonment and deadlock are distinguished on screen; an unanswered dispute does not void a match by default; adjudication is drawn.

title: A guest with no app has no way to drop out, and their sponsor can commit them without asking
description: From the unreachable-guest persona reviewing the new dropping journey in design/journeys. Two findings. (1) All seven steps of dropping/ are John's — a person with an account, holding the app. A guest who joined by link on somebody else's phone cannot reach any roster, so her only exit is texting her sponsor, which dropping/1's own note calls the exact behaviour the product exists to replace. The flakiest people in any group are the ones with no button. (2) In dropping/6 the sponsor taps 'she's in' on the guest's behalf and nothing anywhere asks whether he actually spoke to her. The API is explicit that acting for someone is allowed and always attributed, but attribution is invisible on screen — so a slot can look full when nobody has told the person, which is the precise failure the refusable promotion exists to prevent, reintroduced one step later by a friend's thumb. Related: the persona joined via a link on a FRIEND'S phone, so the push prompt fired on his device; no screen covers joining on a borrowed phone, and rec-friends/4's own note warns that a dishonest reachability report is how a guest stands in a car park on a cancelled Thursday.
acceptance_criteria: A guest-side exit exists that needs no account; relay-answered promotions are visibly attributed and reversible by the guest; joining on a borrowed device is drawn.

title: The whole design system is in px, so a phone with larger text set gets nothing
description: From a 68-year-old 3.5 player persona reviewing design/journeys — six years playing, system text size up two notches, reads her phone at arm's length in sunlight without glasses. Her top finding, verified: every size in the Kitchen Line token file and component CSS is px, and body carried -webkit-text-size-adjust:100% (now removed). A user who has turned their phone's text size up gets no change at all. Fixing it properly is a rem migration across the token file plus every component, not a patch, so it is filed rather than bodged. Her related list of information carried at decorative sizes has been partly patched in the journeys shell (.slot .tag 8.5 to 11px, .notif .acts 9.5 to 11px, .rowline .txt, .ratehero .cnt, .seclbl) but the patch lives in the prototype, not the suite. Also flagged and not fixed: .slot rows are ~25px tall and .queue.mini ~22px, below any reasonable touch target, and groups/2 lists five destinations as slot rows none of which is tappable.
acceptance_criteria: The token file and components use rem, a 200% system text setting is walked through the prototype without breaking layout, and touch targets meet 44px on anything tappable.

title: The rating is a toy inside a rigorous product — no derivation, and DUPR is unacknowledged on DUPR's scale
description: From the competitive-player persona review of design/journeys, the one most likely to pay and most likely to quit. Three findings. (1) comp-friends/6 is billed as 'why the number moved' and is a list of deltas, not a derivation: no opponent rating at time of play, no expected result, no K-factor, no provisional weighting, no margin rule. He can see -0.04 and cannot reconstruct it. (2) The product uses DUPR's own scale - 4.12, 3.96 - and the string DUPR appears nowhere in the prototype. He has a 4.283 DUPR and now holds two four-point-somethings that disagree with no stated relationship. Either import DUPR as a prior and say so (Account.dupr_seed_value exists, D07) or move off that scale. (3) Neither standings table on comp-league/6 carries a games-played column, which is the one denominator rule the product states everywhere else; miss a week and points-for craters with no visible reason. Also unresolved from earlier: 10 of 278 real games finished level and there is still no rule for what a draw does to a rating (pickleball-telegram-bot-1cc).
acceptance_criteria: A per-match rating row shows rating before, opponent rating, expected result and the resulting delta; DUPR's relationship to this number is stated on screen; standings carry games played.

title: EventSeries exists in the schema and is drawn nowhere — no recurring events
description: Two persona reviews landed on this independently. The rec organiser (Dave, 8 friends, twice a week) said the app is a straight no versus WhatsApp and 'flips to yes if the event repeats - a standing Thursday that opens itself and asks the eight of them without me touching it'. The league organiser (Kathy, 16 players, 7 weeks) has no way to build a season: groups/3 shows 'week 6 of 7' and a 'Playoffs top 8' row, but signup/5 only ever creates one event with one starts_wallclock. EventSeries is a v1 table in contract/schema.md and no screen references it. Both real leagues in data/ are 7-week series. This is the single highest-value missing feature for the two personas who would actually organise anything.
acceptance_criteria: A screen creates a recurring event, a screen shows a series and its occurrences, and the league journeys reference the series they are obviously part of.

title: No screen corrects or disputes a score, and the guest+silence path can be gamed
description: Two personas, two angles, same hole. The league organiser would refuse to adopt: 'Somebody will put 11-4 in the wrong side within a fortnight. If I cannot fix it I keep the clipboard as a backup, which is more work than I do today.' contract/api.md has 4.2 amend, 4.4 dispute, 4.5 resolve and 4.6 void, and design/journeys draws none of them - Score.kind='correction' and the dispute path exist only inside a writes block on comp-friends/5. The competitive player found the exploit: sponsor-add creates a Player with account_id NULL from one row, an unclaimed guest cannot confirm, so a match against guests settles on the 72-hour clock with no witness while the account-holder's counted_for_rating is 1. He also noted the selection vector - the proposer picks the intent tag, and drilling removes the scoring surface entirely, so a player can rate the matches they are favoured in and drill the rest.
acceptance_criteria: Amend, dispute and resolve are drawn; and a decision is recorded on whether a match with no account-holding witness may settle on the clock alone.

title: pickleball-social: a group invite 404s when the group has no upcoming event
description:
GET /invites/{token} returns 404 whenever the invite's group has no open event with starts_at >= now.

resolveInvite (server/src/routes/identity.ts) calls nextEventId(), and loadEventSummary returns null when there is no upcoming event, so the handler notFound()s. The InviteView type requires a non-null event.

WHY IT MATTERS: the invite is to a GROUP and is minted with a 14-30 day expiry, but it dies the moment the group's calendar runs dry. Somebody invited last week opens the link and gets exactly the blank a stranger gets — indistinguishable from a revoked or fake link, which is deliberate for strangers and wrong for an invitee.

Observed in production 2026-08-11: the Whitney Ranch Crew invite worked, then 404d three hours after its only event passed. Restored only by inserting new events.

FIX SHAPE: make InviteView.event nullable and render 'you are in, nothing is scheduled yet' at the guest door — joining a group should not require a game to exist. Joining an event stays event-scoped.
acceptance_criteria: An invite to a group with zero upcoming events resolves 200 and the guest door lets the person join the group; joining still works once an event exists; a revoked/expired/nonexistent token still renders identically to the stranger case.

title: Contract blockers: 6 product calls before backend build
description: The contract at pickleball-social/contract/ surfaced 31 open questions. Six need a product decision before the server track can build: OQ-06 (does a score count immediately or at settlement - conflicts with D06), OQ-08 (do guest matches move ratings - two sheets say yes, one says no), OQ-45 (void threshold: unanimity vs 2-of-4), OQ-47 (is there a public match link at all - D17 vs sheet 04), OQ-16 (does a session inherit the event's pinned courts - the D16 pin is currently discarded at session start, in nobody's plan), OQ-33 (cast has two names and two inverted ratings per person across sheets). The rest are answerable during the build.
acceptance_criteria: Six decisions recorded in the contract; contract promoted from draft to v1.
close_reason: All six resolved in contract/decisions.md with reasoning and reversal costs. Notable: OQ-08 resolved AGAINST sheet 04 (guest matches count, damped) because sheet 04's 'nothing to compare against' assumed guests are unmodelled, which foundation 1 rejects. OQ-45 resolved as neither sheet proposed: one-from-each-side, defeating both the unresponsive-fourth and collusive-pair failure modes. OQ-16: the pin governs the roster, not round 1.

title: Overprint prototype suite: 8-sheet journey + edge-case map
description:
Design direction S5 'Overprint' selected by user. Building an 8-sheet HTML prototype at pickleball-social/design/prototype/ mapping every journey, state and edge case before any app code is written.

Sheets: index (map/IA), 01 week, 02 people, 03 session (round robin), 04 scores/ratings/social, 05 courts/access, 06 privacy/states, 07 decision register.

Shared contract in _BRIEF.md; tokens extracted verbatim from direction-S5-print.html into _overprint-tokens.css.

acceptance_criteria: All 8 sheets built, AA contrast verified in both themes, no horizontal scroll at 390-1440px, 15 decisions documented with recommendations.
close_reason: 8-sheet Overprint prototype complete: 330+ screens, 38 sheet-level forks, 18 cross-cutting decisions. Headless-audited to 0 AA failures and 0 overflow across both themes and 5 breakpoints.

title: Hybrid organizer: multi-group, multi-event, web+SMS front door
description: Approved plan at ~/.claude/plans/so-between-this-and-replicated-cocoa.md. One Worker, one shared roster, two front doors: Telegram groups (buttons+DMs) and a first-class web app (phone/SMS-OTP identity, SMS notifications). Multi-group, multi-event with proposals; absorbs pickleball-singles-bot.

title: Waitlist promotion notifications (you're now confirmed)
description: When a drop promotes someone from the waitlist onto a confirmed court, tell that person directly instead of leaving it buried in the roster edit.
design: Promotion detection already exists: describeCascade() compares court assignment before vs after and builds a 'moves up to Court N' list — it just builds strings, so change it to return the player objects. Then per promoted player: DM if opted in (dm:<userId>), else group @mention via mention(). Message: 'Someone dropped out — you're now confirmed on Court N' + a Drop button. CONDITIONAL TAIL: if nobody is behind them (no waitlist players after the confirmed courts), add a gentle heads-up that dropping now would leave the court short. Guests (g:) have no Telegram identity — notify their SPONSOR instead ('your guest X is now confirmed'). Web-only signups (w:) cannot be notified at all.
acceptance_criteria: A drop that promotes a waitlisted player notifies that player (DM or @mention) with their new court, a drop action, and a waitlist-depth-aware warning.

title: Singles bot: finish Telegram setup (BotFather, secrets, webhook, /setup)
description: The singles bot (../pickleball-singles-bot) is deployed to https://pickleball-singles-bot.jmartin84.workers.dev with its own KV namespace (1f10c3e599a141f8927223af7d34d003) and cron. Remaining manual steps (need the user's Telegram account): 1) @BotFather /newbot (e.g. Whitney Singles Bot), copy token; /setprivacy -> Disable. 2) In ../pickleball-singles-bot: npx wrangler secret put TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and npx wrangler secret put WEBHOOK_SECRET (openssl rand -hex 32). 3) Register webhook: curl 'https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/setWebhook?url=https://pickleball-singles-bot.jmartin84.workers.dev/webhook&secret_token=<SECRET>'. 4) Add bot to singles group, make admin, send /setup. 5) Verify /in confirms Court 1 at 2 players; test /run?slot=rollcall&key=<SECRET> on a game-eve. NOTE: to free a cron slot, the cron on padlepicker-discover-manufacturers was removed (was '0 12 * * *') — restore it if that job is still needed.

title: Hero tally: reward the player who fills the deciding spot
description: Self-contained, zero Telegram-platform friction — recommended to build first.
design: KV: hero:<userId> -> count (or one 'heroes' object). Credit when a join flips a court from partial->confirmed (fills the 4th slot), detectable by comparing groupPlayersIntoCourts() before vs after in the add path (addMember / callback 'in'). Display: star badge next to name in rosterText and/or a /heroes leaderboard command. Only Telegram members (u:<id>) can be credited; web sign-ups have no identity.
acceptance_criteria: Filling the 4th slot of a court increments that user's tally; tally is visible (badge and/or /heroes).

description: Cold review 2026-08-12, Apple-bar gap #2: groups/1 renders a nav list then adds a full-width OPEN THURSDAY ADV button duplicating a row; native iOS trusts the row + chevron affordance. The deck's right-edge-chevron grammar exists (goes-somewhere rows); the double-writing is where the 'over the top' feeling now comes from after the copy cut. Also 'ANSWER NEEDED' (groups/1) vs 'THEY NEED AN ANSWER' (home/1) — same state, two phrasings. The same drill-down (full game history) is labelled ALL SEVEN (home/2), EVERY GAME (you/1) and EVERYTHING (profile/1); drill-friends/2's SEND IT has no visible recipient or channel; rec-friends/4's SEND IT THROUGH JOHN is uninterpretable in 2 seconds (note: that label is register-protected from the copy audit — commit bde6f7fe says it states what actually happens — so this is a design reconciliation, not a mechanical rename). Remaining design work on this issue: wire 'I need a sub' into the sub-ask flow (currently still writes declined and stops, per D28); decide LET JOHN TELL ME vs the register-protected 'Send it through John'; the visual confirm affordance (tick / row highlight) the client sketched lives with h48.

The label is now 'Who won'; the real fix is rendering the rows as controls in the deck's offset-block-edge button grammar with the reporter's winning side preselected. In design/journeys/index.html, the score-entry screens under rec-friends (and their organiser/disputes siblings). Related: 4s2 (no text input drawn anywhere).

title: No organiser view of the round robin: no draw preview, no pinned pairing, no seeding
description: From a 5.0 persona who runs a 12-16 player invitational round robin and a monthly ladder on a spreadsheet with her own rotation algorithm. She said the rotation quality itself matches her spreadsheet - comp-rr/4's 56 distinct pairings with zero repeats, 119 of 120 possible pairs over five weeks, checkable rather than asserted. What is missing is her. comp-rr/1 gives one button, 'Start game 1', and comp-rr/2 shows the draw already committed: no preview, no regenerate, no way to pin a pairing she wants tested. No seeding anywhere - court 1 is an ordinal, not the top court, so 4.0s and 5.0s shuffle flat, which she called the loudest complaint she would get. Rotation is also the only format; fixed_partners is a reserved enum with no generator. Named as the ONE thing that flips her verdict from 'part of it' to yes. Three smaller gaps from the same review: comp-rr/6 draws exactly one sitter when 13-14 players means two or three every game; no screen shows a per-player sit-out count, so the fairness rule is stated but not auditable; and groups/4 offers audience 'Just who I ask' while no name picker exists on any screen, so her weekly 16-of-30 invite list cannot be expressed.
acceptance_criteria: An organiser previews, adjusts and commits a draw; seeding is expressible; sit-out counts are visible per player; the 'just who I ask' picker exists.

title: The product computes a rating and refuses to use it for matching
description: Independently reached by a 5.0 tournament player and a never-played beginner from opposite ends, which is why it is worth recording. The 5.0: nothing in 102 screens helps him find a game at his level; entry/6 says 'all welcome', rec-open says 'all levels welcome', comp-friends/2 offers Competitive/Chill/Drills and no level, and organiser/2 sorts subs by acceptances. Level lives only in group NAMES. The beginner: 'Thursday Adv 4.0-4.5' on home/5 and dropping/2 was the single string that would stop him turning up - '4.0-4.5 of what?' - and no screen anywhere explains what the scale means, where the floor is, or where 'fine' sits. So the same undrawn concept simultaneously blocks the strongest player from finding a good game and the weakest from daring to join a normal one. Note this is a deliberate-looking absence, not an oversight: rating-based matching has real social costs and D17's people-search rules constrain it. It needs a recorded decision either way rather than silence.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on rating-based level signalling, and if yes, an event states its level in something other than its name.

title: The uncertainty band is required by INV-9 and drawn on no screen
description: From the 5.0 tournament-player review of design/journeys. Rating.uncertainty exists in schema.md and INV-9 states a provisional rating is 'drawn as a band, not a point'. No screen draws one - not you/1, not profile/1, not even you/2 where the player has one game of ten. A 4.12 over 68 games and a 4.12 over 11 games render identically, which is precisely the distinction the field exists to express. Related from the same review: RatingEvent.explanation is capped at 'rung 2 - never publish coefficients', so you/3 ranks inputs and withholds weights; the reviewer's word for that was 'inspectable, not auditable' - he cannot recompute the 62% expected-win figure the screen shows him. And schema.md badges seeded_from_dupr as 'Seeded' until match 10; that badge is on no screen either.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional ratings render as a band; the Seeded badge appears where a DUPR seed is in effect.

title: A league season has no playoff, and no screen sets the response deadline
description: From a league-organiser persona re-review of design/journeys, after she said she would switch her league over for weeks 1-7 and put week 8 back on paper. Two gaps. (1) groups/5 creates a recurring event with '4 weeks / keep going / a season', and groups/3 shows a 'Playoffs - top 8' row that nothing builds; both real Las Vegas leagues in data/ are 7 weeks then a bracket seeded from the standings. (2) groups/2 and organiser/1 both reference an answer-by-Wednesday deadline and no screen sets it; Event.roster_closes_at exists in schema.md and is drawn nowhere. Also noted and smaller: no screen anywhere shows how a score number is actually typed - organiser/4, disputes/2 and comp-league/4 all draw the numbers pre-filled with no keypad, stepper or field.
acceptance_criteria: A season can be built with a playoff seeded from standings; roster_closes_at is set on a screen; and one score-entry screen shows the actual input.
notes: 2026-08-12: score keypad/text-input stays out of the polish pass by scope agreement (polish existing screens only). The 'Tap a name — winners first' label was reduced to 'Who won'; the row-affordance redesign is filed separately.

title: An organiser removing a member is the last thing the product does TO somebody, and it is undrawn
description: Named by a UX re-review as the single most important remaining gap in design/journeys, after signing off on everything else. groups/7 asserts removal is organiser-only in every invite_mode, D10 calls it irreversible (adding a person is reversible, removing one is not), groups/8 draws only voluntary leaving, and path-organiser ends on the screen that names the power without ever drawing its use. It is the only remaining case where the product does something TO a person rather than for them, which makes it the one most in need of the care the rest of the set gets: what the organiser sees before confirming, what the removed person sees, whether they are told at all, and the fact that they may still write a Score for a match in progress they are a participant in, because authorisation for score entry is participation and never membership. Ranked after it: failure states (no offline entry, no lost race on start-round, no expired link in 102 screens), capacity overflow (rec-friends/3 insists 'not a waiting list' and person 17 of 16 at open play has no screen), and editing a proposal.
acceptance_criteria: Removal is drawn from both sides, and the removed person's surviving rights are on the screen rather than only in the contract.

title: Nothing in the product knows that time has passed — no dormancy, no rating staleness, no quiet way back
description: From a returning-player persona reviewing design/journeys — played 3x a week for four months, tore a calf, six months out, now cleared. Her findings. (1) After six months the first screen is home/6 'Quiet week', which is honest and cold: the app thinks she had a quiet WEEK. Nothing anywhere says it has been a while. (2) you/1 shows 4.12 with a +0.06 delta from a match in February, presented as current, with no date and no staleness marker — and profile/2 shows that number to everyone she shares a group with. She wants it greyed with 'last played 12 Feb' or held pending a few games back. (3) The only acknowledgement of elapsed time anywhere in 118 screens is the 'Last played 6 Aug' subtitle on a groups/1 row. (4) home/4 draws a FORWARD gap as a tappable band; there is no backwards equivalent. (5) No season archive — if her league rolled over, her 257 and her 13th place are simply on no screen. (6) Worst: the only way back in is groups/4, which broadcasts a proposal to fifteen people after six months of silence. There is no quiet re-entry — no way to take an open slot on something already happening. Her verdict: 'the app never noticed I left, so it cannot notice I am back.' Note the product is right not to record absence as a fault (dropping/2 deliberately stores no counter); this is about elapsed time, not reliability.
acceptance_criteria: A returning-user state exists, rating staleness is visible to the owner and to viewers, and there is a way back in that does not require proposing.

title: No organiser operational view, and no subs flow
description: From the league-organiser persona review of design/journeys (16 players, 4 courts, 7 games, 7 weeks, currently a clipboard and an Excel workbook). The only organiser screen in 111 is groups/6 Settings - invite mode, requires_recording, who can remove - which is governance, not operations. She needs one board at 8:40pm with a phone in one hand: who has answered and who has not, which courts have a score in and which do not. comp-league/3 shows all four courts but it is a player's screen. Separately, comp-league/1 has a 'Send a sub' button that goes nowhere and no sub flow exists anywhere; finding subs when two drop on the day is her second-worst pain of the week. She also noted that availability shows a COUNT (14 of 16) and never the two names who have not answered, so she is back to texting blind, and that no screen anywhere shows how a score number is actually typed - comp-league/4 draws the score pre-filled with no keypad, stepper or field.
acceptance_criteria: An organiser night-view exists; a sub request flow exists or the button is removed; availability names the silent; a score-entry screen shows the actual input.

title: Nothing is designed for the beginner's day one, and 'the kitchen' actively misleads
description: From the beginner persona review of design/journeys - nine weeks into playing, invited by a friend, no league experience. Three concrete findings. (1) There is no beginner state of the You tab: you/1 is John with 109 games, and nobody has drawn what a person sees on day one. Her rating is 'withheld' but that word only appears in the state panel, never on a screen - so she sees other people's numbers and an absence where hers should be, and an unexplained absence reads as 'not good enough yet' louder than a small number would. (2) 'In the kitchen - can't be changed' was misread for a full minute by the one reviewer who actually knows the sport: the kitchen is the non-volley zone, and borrowing a familiar word for an unfamiliar meaning is worse than a new word. A UX review reached the same conclusion independently. Recommend 'Settled - can't be changed' in copy, keeping kitchen paint as the visual zone. (3) 'Your spot doesn't move. People ahead of you can drop; you only ever go up' was written to reassure and does the opposite - it tells a beginner there is an order and she is near the bottom of it. Also: rec-friends/6 pre-selects the reader as the winner, which she called mortifying, and rec-friends/5 leads with 'Singles - two of you play', which excludes the third person with no way to say who sits.
acceptance_criteria: A day-one You screen exists; the withheld rating explains itself on screen at the moment of joining; the kitchen copy decision is recorded either way.

title: api.md has no section 8.2, and notification categories are never enumerated
description: Found while designing the push-permission screen for design/journeys (rec-friends/4). api.md section 8 jumps straight from 8.1 (the reachability ladder and the relay) to 8.3 (push registration). There is no 8.2. Separately, 8.4 says 'Defaults are logistics-on, engagement-off' and PUT /notification-preferences takes a 'category' field, but no catalogue of categories exists anywhere in the contract. This matters beyond tidiness: the consent copy on the permission screen promises 'only about games you are in, nothing else, ever', and that promise is only honest if logistics-only is genuinely the default and the category list is closed. OQ-23 (court_broke unmutable while on a roster) also references categories that are not defined.
acceptance_criteria: api.md gains a section 8.2 defining the notification category enum, which categories are logistics vs engagement, and which are unmutable while on a roster; the permission-screen copy in design/journeys is checked against it.

title: declined -> in keeps the original position, letting a decliner jump the queue
description: Opened by D28 (2026-08-11). RosterEntry has a UNIQUE index on (event_id, player_id) and position is NOT NULL and write-once, so changing your mind is a state transition on one row and the original position survives. Somebody who declined at position 3 and re-enters at 7pm therefore sits ahead of four people who said yes in between. Options: a nullable re-entry position, a separate re_entered_at ordering key, or accept it and say so on the screen. Note dropped -> in has carried the identical problem since v1 and was never decided; declining makes it far more likely to be hit because declining is cheap and dropping is not.
acceptance_criteria: A rule is recorded in the decision register, schema.md's RosterEntry cascade invariants reflect it, and a schema test covers re-entry ordering.

title: Standings must carry the league's own metric, not just win-loss
description: Found by putting the real league sheets into design/journeys (comp-league/6 shows it). Both Las Vegas leagues rank on POINTS FOR per player - 11 a game, 77 a night, summed over the season - not on games won. Ranking the same 33 games by record instead moves John Martin from 13th to 8th and Josh Wong from 12th to 4th. Neither ordering is wrong; they answer different questions. GET /groups/{id}/standings currently implies one metric. It needs a metric selector (points_for | record | per-round differential) with the group's own metric as the default, so a league recognises its own table while the app can still rate players honestly. Both remain computed at read time - storing either would make the other look like a bug.
acceptance_criteria: api.md documents the standings metric parameter and its default; Group (or EventSeries) carries the league's metric; the two orderings are reproducible from the same match rows.

title: A drawn game has no rating rule, and win_by 2 never applies
description: Found by putting the real league sheets into design/journeys. Across 278 recorded court results in the two Las Vegas Adv 4.0-4.5 leagues (Bill Briare Thursday, Police Memorial Saturday, weeks 1-5 of 7): TEN games finished level, and ZERO went past 11. MatchSide.is_winner is nullable so a drawn match is representable, but the rating model has win and loss and nothing else - rating_event needs a delta and there is no rule for a draw. 10/278 is 3.6 percent, not a rounding error, and choosing a rule after ratings ship means recomputing the ledger. Separately, Session.target_points/win_by default to 11 and 2; these leagues play to 11 capped with ties allowed, so win_by needs to accept 1 and the default should be reconsidered.
acceptance_criteria: A rule for drawn matches is recorded in the decision register and reflected in schema.md's rating section; Session.win_by's default and legal values are restated to cover capped play. design/journeys comp-league/4 loses its GAP badge.

title: Event has nowhere to record what a drilling session is working on
description: Surfaced by design/journeys (drill-friends step 2, flagged with a GAP badge). A drilling session is defined by its focus - 'third-shot drops, then cross-court dinks' - and Event in contract/schema.md has no free-text field: id, group_id, series_id, venue_id, starts_at, starts_wallclock, tz, courts, per_court, proposed_by_player_id, intent_tags, audience, state, roster_closes_at, rated_default, cancellation fields, handed_over_to_player_id. Nothing else in the journeys prototype maps to a column that does not exist; this one does. Decide between a nullable Event.note text column and an intent_tags extension, then update schema.md and add a migration.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded in contract/README.md's register, schema.md reflects it, and the GAP badge in design/journeys/data.js is replaced with a real table and column name.

title: Web push notifications (replaces Twilio SMS plan?)
description: PWA push via VAPID: generate keypair (store as Worker secrets), push-subscription storage per user in KV, notifyUser gains a 'push' channel. Free, no A2P registration. iOS requires the PWA installed to home screen first. If this lands well, P6 phone-OTP identity can use it instead of SMS — decide then whether Twilio is still needed.

title: P6: Web first-class — phone OTP login, p:<phone> players, SMS notices
description: otp:/session:/webuser: KV; rate-limited OTP; join/drop/propose from web as p:<phoneE164>; access travels by shared event links (no directory); one viewer-auth helper for initData+session.
notes: Deferred by user choice until Twilio A2P registration completes — P7 (web app UI) built first.

title: P5: Notification fan-out + Twilio SMS channel
description: notifyUser routes u:->dmUser, p:->sendSms (Twilio REST via fetch; secrets TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID/AUTH_TOKEN/FROM). Category prefs apply to both. NOTE: start A2P/toll-free registration EARLY - days of lead time; trial reaches only verified numbers.
close_reason: Deployed 652802ad; seam live, /test-sms gated 403 verified; real SMS blocked on user Twilio registration

title: P3: Multi-group, onboard singles group, retire fork
description: Drop bound-chat gate; /setdays, /setpercourt; member:<userId> tracking; migrate_to_chat_id re-key. Cutover Whitney Ranch singles group; deleteWebhook on fork; archive pickleball-singles-bot (frees a cron against the 5-cron account cap).
close_reason: Deployed b915a6bb. Code side complete; group cutover is a manual step documented in the commit.

title: P4: Proposals — /propose, per-event callbacks, cancel
description: kind:proposed events; in:<eid>/out:<eid>/guest:<eid>; 4-char pid in callback_data (64-byte limit); tombstone cancel + notify; /status lists all.

title: Telegram Mini App: per-user roster view with real styling
description:
The only way to get true per-user UI in Telegram: a Web App button opens our existing styled /signup page inside Telegram. Solves the two things a shared group message cannot do — showing '(me)' next to your own name, and showing different buttons to people already on the roster.

## Context
A normal group message is ONE shared message: identical text and identical inline keyboard for every viewer. Per-user personalization is impossible there. A Mini App is the supported escape hatch.
design: Add a Web App button (web_app: {url}) to the roster keyboard. Telegram passes initData (signed with the bot token) identifying the viewer — verify the HMAC server-side, then render a personalized view: '(me)' badge, and contextual actions (someone on the roster sees 'I can no longer go', someone off it sees 'I'm in'). Reuses signupPageHtml + gives full CSS control. Requires HTTPS (already) and initData validation.
notes: Server side BUILT + deployed (a2dfc43a): verifyInitData() HMAC-SHA256 validation, personalised /signup view with (me) badge + contextual button, Mini App actions act as u:<id>. Verified: forged initData -> 403, anonymous view unchanged. REMAINING: BotFather — create a Direct Link Mini App (/newapp) pointing at https://pickleball-bot.jmartin84.workers.dev/signup, then set CONFIG.miniAppUrl to the resulting https://t.me/<bot>/<app> link. Until then the roster button opens the external browser, where initData is empty and the page correctly falls back to anonymous.

title: Attendance & drop-off analytics (who's flaky vs committed)
description:
Track per-person attendance and drop behavior over time to see who's reliable. Internal-only; may not be circulated.

## Context
SENSITIVE: this is behavioral data about real people (a reliability score). Store privately, don't expose on the public /signup page, be thoughtful about surfacing it socially.
design: Data model: stats keyed by Telegram user id (stats:<userId>) and/or an append-only per-week history:<date> event log. Capture events: in (signup), out (drop), LATE drop (out after cutoff/final = strongest flakiness signal), inclusion on the locked FINAL roster (= expected to attend). True attendance/no-show needs a ground-truth signal the bot doesn't have yet — add a post-game 'who showed up?' prompt or let the organizer mark no-shows. Reliable only for Telegram members (u:) and guests (tied to inviter); web sign-ups (w:) are name-only with no stable cross-week identity — another reason to join.
acceptance_criteria: Per-user counts of signups, drops, late drops, and final-roster appearances are recorded across weeks and viewable by the organizer.

title: Cohort nudges as group @mentions (confirmed / waitlist)
description: Extend sendRecruitingAlert()/cutoff to @mention cohorts with action buttons.
design: Confirmed cohort: group post @mentioning confirmed players + Drop button ('can't make it? free your spot'). Waitlist cohort: @mention waitlisters ('you're #N of M; K more unlock Court X; recruit via /guest or Drop'). Prefer ONE combined post to reduce spam. Only players with a Telegram id can be @mentioned; web names get a generic line. mention() already pings via tg://user?id=.
acceptance_criteria: At cutoff (or on command), a group message @mentions the right cohorts with working Drop/Claim buttons.

title: Targeted nudges + save-the-day hero tally
description: Engagement features: cohort-targeted nudge messages (confirmed / waitlist / unsigned) and a hero tally that rewards the player who fills the deciding 4th spot. See ROADMAP.md for full feasibility analysis. Delivery is constrained by Telegram Bot API: bots cannot cold-DM users, cannot enumerate group members, and web sign-ups have no Telegram identity — so most nudges must be group @mentions, not private DMs.

title: Decide whether design data/ workbooks get committed
description: design/../data/ holds the two real league xlsx workbooks (Saturday Adv, Thursday Adv) that the journeys deck's names and figures come from. They are untracked; the journeys README calls committing them 'a call worth making deliberately' (privacy: real player names). Decide and either commit or .gitignore them. They were accidentally staged and removed from a commit on 2026-08-12.

title: Promote lime-button structural tokens (--btn-frame) into the token file
description: The WHICH LIME IS A BUTTON rule text is now a dated amendment in design/prototype-kitchenline/_kitchenline-tokens.css (2026-08-12), with stated exceptions (OS notification chrome, prototype shell controls). Still open: the structural values themselves (3px standoff/frame, offset-plate collapse) live as magic numbers in the journeys shell CSS; if a second artifact adopts the rule, extract --btn-frame etc. into the token file properly. Also unadjudicated by the rule text: .rate-delta (inset, unframed, non-tappable lime chip) and the home/4 kitband CTA (kitchen paint carrying a tappable row — 'kitchen is never a button' breach that P20 protects as the scheduling aid; needs a deliberate design call).

title: Points labels drawn four ways; 'Put a score in' screen sits under You in comp-friends
description: Cohesion sweep leftovers in design/journeys/index.html, deliberately not fixed mechanically: (1) points labelled '61 pts' vs 'you: 61' vs bare '247' vs '349 · 6 weeks' across ledger/standings rows — needs one grammar chosen by a design eye, not a regex. (2) The comp-friends 'Put a score in' screen carries tab You while the identical player action under comp-league carries tab Play; the deck's own rule says entering a score lives under Play with the game, but changing the lit tab without a tab tap would reintroduce the silent-tab-flip bug the a11y round killed — needs the journey step restructured, not just the tab flag flipped. (3) Attendance said three ways: '16 players · 7 games' / 'Who was there / 16' / '13 in' badges.

title: Commercial venue needs are entirely absent — decide whether that is a scope decision
description: From the venue-manager persona review of design/journeys (8 courts, ~900 members, four open plays a day). The drop-in flow itself is good - entry/6 to rec-open/2 is fast and happens on the player's phone, and he would put the QR on his wall. Everything else commercial is missing: payments, waivers, check-in, no-show tracking, court booking (Venue is expectations-only per D12), any report at all, comms to a membership, coach/clinic management, and a staff or tablet view. Membership is binary - member or not - with no dues, expiry, lapsed state, tier, member-only event or member price. Insurance is the sharpest: he must know who was in the building, and rec-open/2 collects one first name with no surname, no waiver and no emergency contact, so the clipboard stays. His conclusion: 'a very good app for the four people on a Sunday; for eight courts and 900 members it is the paddle rack digitised.' He accepted the player half of D17 and would fight the venue half - his argument is that an event a business publishes is not a person, so a venue-published event with no roster and no names is not a people-search. That is a real argument and worth a recorded yes or no rather than silence.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on whether commercial venues are in scope for v1, and if so whether D17 admits a venue-published event.

title: Journeys prototype: consolidate 70 steps to ~45 and add the promotion/relay journey
description: Two UX/content reviews (2026-08-11) found duplication in design/journeys: three separate screens argue 'there is no discovery endpoint' (home/6, entry/7, drill-open/2); three different chromes draw the same score-entry form (rec-friends/5, comp-league/4, comp-friends/4); two standings screens (comp-league/6, comp-rr/7); four of entry's seven doors are states of one join screen now that the graph is navigable; feed/4 and feed/6 are arguments rather than screens and belong in the contract. Separately the largest coverage gap is untouched: waitlist promotion + the sponsor relay, which the contract calls the single most valuable notification in the product and which exercises INV-4's pin, D16's named cost, D14's relay and the derived notification audience together. Disputes, cancellation/handover and the organiser's own view are also absent - no journey has an organiser as its 'who'.
acceptance_criteria: Step count is materially reduced with no argument lost, and a promotion/relay journey exists showing the pin transaction, a refusable promotion and a sponsor-relayed notification.
notes: 2026-08-12 polish pass: score rendering now has one inline form — SC() joins SCORE(); all thirteen .match rows, both lock-screen titles, and every running-copy score converted; spaced/literal dashes normalized. Step-count consolidation itself remains open.

title: P7: Mini App event picker + propose form + membership checks
description: startapp deep links (trusted via signed initData start_param); group picker from member:<userId>; SECURITY: every mutation verifies membership (getChatMember / webuser.groups).
close_reason: Deployed 0662a61e; live checks pass. Group picker from member:<userId> deferred to P6 (needs multi-group reality).

title: Guest claim-link: let an invitee claim their guest spot
description:
When a member adds a guest, let them send the guest a link to claim the spot themselves — another nudge to join Telegram.

## Context
Flagged as complex/nice-to-have by the user. Depends on guest model already in place (/guest, /unguest).
design: On /guest, mint a claim token stored in KV (claim:<token> -> {date, inviterId, guestName}). Share via Telegram deep link (t.me/<bot>?start=claim_<token>) or a /signup/claim?token= web URL. Claiming converts the g:<inviterId>:<name> entry to the claimer's own identity (u:<id> if they join Telegram) so the guest becomes self-managing. Handle token expiry, one-time use, and key/cascade conversion.
notes: DESIGN SUPERSEDED — no claim token needed. Use a unique single-use GROUP INVITE LINK per guest placeholder: createChatInviteLink(member_limit=1, name=<placeholder>) when the guest is added. Telegram reports ChatMemberUpdated.invite_link ('Chat invite link, which was used by the user to join the chat') on join, so the bot maps link -> placeholder and renames it to the real user in place (u:<id>, clear guestOf). Collapses claim+join into ONE tap. PREREQS: bot must be group admin with can_invite_users, and the webhook must be re-registered with allowed_updates including 'chat_member' (verified: NOT sent by default). Edge case: a guest already in the group fires no join event, so no auto-claim — they tap I'm in and the sponsor clears the placeholder.

title: Private DM opt-in onboarding (optional)
description:
Enables real DMs instead of group @mentions — only worth it if people want personal reminders.

## Context
Blocks the 'message unsigned group members individually' idea — not achievable; substitute a group broadcast + Claim button.
design: Telegram bots cannot cold-DM: users must Start the bot in DM first. Add opt-in flow, store dm:<userId> -> private chat_id in KV. Then nudges DM opted-in users, falling back to group @mention. Still cannot reach unsigned members who never interacted (no member-list API).

value: Cloudflare account hit the 5-cron free-tier limit when deploying pickleball-singles-bot (2026-07-24). Freed a slot by removing the cron from padlepicker-discover-manufacturers (was '0 12 * * *') via the API. Current cron users: padlepicker-affiliate-link-health (*/15), padlepicker-daily-housekeeping (0 4), padlepicker-price-refresh (*/10), pickleball-bot (*/15), pickleball-singles-bot (*/15).

Design constraint discovered via the Cold Issue (Bond 2050) direction study, 2026-08-06: a player's name must never be rendered next to a fault/error colour or failure language. Dropping out early is the behaviour the drop-and-cascade mechanic depends on; any visual language that renders a withdrawal as failure (red, 'COMPROMISED', broken-streak graphics) discourages the single most valuable social behaviour in the product. Applies to every design direction. This is foundation #8 (NOT #7 — a numbering swap propagated from _BRIEF.md was corrected everywhere on 2026-08-12; canonical numbering is prototype-kitchenline/index.html: #7 = list is the record, #8 = no name beside a fault colour).

Journeys deck (pickleball-social/design/journeys/): the deck is MOBILE-FIRST and possibly mobile-only per the client, 2026-08-12 — desk mode exists but wider sizes are explicitly not a priority. index.html and artifact.html must stay in lockstep; regenerate artifact.html mechanically (awk: drop lines 1-35 and the </head>/<body>/</body>/</html> lines), never dual-edit; correct diff is 39 chrome lines. The 2026-08-12 polish pass added: fitCourtNames() (measured name-shortening on the court plate, 104-unit lane, degrade full -> First L -> truncated), SC(a,b) (the inline score form, no verdict paint), .slot.ask/.slot.lead row grammar, and the WHICH LIME IS A BUTTON amendment in _kitchenline-tokens.css.

Product vocabulary idea from the Kitchen Line (P1) direction study, 2026-08-06: map the sport's own non-volley zone ('the kitchen') onto the app's immutability rule. Pickleball already has a named zone where a different rule applies; the product already has locked state (played rounds, confirmed courts, recorded history are immutable per decision D04 and BRIEF 4.1). Naming the locked/no-edit state 'the kitchen' gives the app native sport vocabulary instead of generic UI language. Also from P1: 'every score is two sides across a net, never a hyphen on one line' as a layout rule. See pickleball-social/design/direction-P1-court.html.

Design constraint from the direction studies, 2026-08-06: the ordered 1-8 roster queue must always be printed as a numbered list, no matter what spatial metaphor a design uses. Rings, panel grids and 2x2 court blocks cannot encode sequence, and sequence is the product's core mechanic. The graphic is the summary; the list is the record; if they disagree the list wins. Consistent with decision D16. This is foundation #7 (NOT #8 — numbering corrected 2026-08-12; canonical is prototype-kitchenline/index.html: #7 = list is the record, #8 = no name beside a fault colour).

Contract v1 for the pickleball social app lives at pickleball-social/contract/ (README, schema, api, fixtures, open-questions, decisions). Stack ratified 2026-08-08: Expo/React Native client (iOS+Android+web), Cloudflare Workers + D1 + Durable Objects backend, Firebase Auth + FCM for identity and push. NO phone numbers, NO SMS, NO Twilio. Telegram is out of the product entirely; the bot runs the real Thursday game only until the app reaches parity, then retires. Because SMS is gone, reachability is a property that can be false and the sponsor relay is a first-class notification path: when a guest has no reachable channel, their sponsor is messaged to pass it on.
